When trying to move her hands, she didn't know herself; when trying to make a sound, she didn't realize either.  
Across the fence and across the moonlight, if that bachelor had any sense, he would have accepted the rice cake.  
He accepted the rice cake, put it aside, held the little hand, and trembled.  
In the mountains, the eldest child is like three, three, and the southeast wind blows, making sidesteps.  
Did the southeast wind blow and make sidesteps? No, he made sidesteps to see the bachelor.  
Flywheel spins round and round with a twist, the bachelor at the smiling house is hit by the early morning dew.  
The sun sets in the western mountains, and the moon rises over Wolchuldong Peak.  
Will the old bracken come up? Will the late bracken come up?  
Make a fence out of bracken and hang a gate with daylilies.  
Wearing a paulownia-colored jeogori and a horsehair headband, not even a speck is stained, went to the pawnshop.  
When the mother-in-law died, it felt so comfortable, but when barley pounding started, memories came back.  
The hometown where I lived became a foreign land, and the hometown where my beloved lives became my hometown.  
The sun sets in the western mountains, and the moon rises over Wolchuldong Peak.  
In Samgaksan Mountain’s valley, the rain drizzles here and there, a young child sleeps in the eldest's arms.  
Beyond that mountain ridge, leaving my wife behind, walking the night path is hard.  
Across the fence and across the moonlight, if that bachelor has any sense, he would accept the rice cake.  
The bride stayed too long, just locking the door and only sleeping.  
If she slept, did she really sleep? Listen carefully to her breathing and come in step.  
They say the bride only goes out at night, while the bachelor goes to the village tavern in broad daylight.  
If the bride stays too long, she leaves the four main gates open and sleeps lightly.  
Opening the south gate and sweeping the courtyard, even the changed mountains and rivers brighten again.  
The sun sets, darkness comes, and smoke rises from every valley.  
Let's light the lantern and go to visit the beloved’s room for fun.  
Beloved, please serve me often; I too will serve you often.  
Plant rice seedlings in this field, and the leaves flutter beautifully, how splendid it is!", '@Uhuh Uhah Eheyi Uho

Tattletale, Armenian,

The little dog will bite him,
The little bird will peck him,
That comes from all that clicking.

Steps up, steps down,
You don’t get this or that from your life again.
Little bite, little kiss, little step,
Fire in the drawer;
Also, smoke, amen.
Tomorrow the stalls come;
The day after tomorrow won’t be,
Then we get a big piece of cake. Amen.

N.N. I baptize you,
The water covers you,
The water pours on you,
N.N. I name you.
I swing, I swing, I swing in peace;
Whoever likes, swings along with Frederik:
I have fulfilled my duties at school,
Now I swing happily, now I swing softly.

I swing, I swing, I swing joyfully;
Who is sweet, may the swinging bring joy;
Who does evil, swinging won’t make him truly happy;
Who is good and diligent, he swings with me.

Dancing, jumping,
Cheerfully singing
Express a joyful spirit
And therefore stand well as children.

Who can jump,
Who can jump
If he, stubborn, lazy or bad,
Has committed a bad deed?

“That’s why I sing,
That’s why I jump,”
Says little Jet while dancing,
Who sets her little feet with pleasure.
Who has to stay at school for a long time,
For him, it seems,
Reading and writing
Soon become boring.

Sometimes banishing care,
Makes one cheerful and content.
A bow, too strongly drawn,
Easily snaps apart.

Blessed are we that learning,
Free from slavish torment,
If we diligently resist,
Is replaced by play!

Then one sees us satisfied,
When the break is over,
Stepping cheerfully back to school,
Then the song rings out happily again:

“Playing all day
Would also, it seems,
Bore us in the long run;
There must be variety.”
There went a little man over the bridge,
With seven cats on his back,
And every cat had seven kittens:
Ra, ra, how many legs crossed the bridge?
Two legs sat on three legs,
Then came four legs and wanted to bite three legs,
Then two legs took three legs,
To throw at four legs.
Witje, Witje sat on the rack,
Witje, Witje broke his neck,
And there is no carpenter
Who can fix Witje, Witje.
There stands a lady in the door,
With a white scarf in front,
The more she stands there,
The more she fades away.
A wooden little house,
A copper little safe,
An iron turn in the hole:
Ra, ra, what is that?", "Belongs together Sailors all as one,
Who were by the Sea,
Are you caught by storm or distress
God helps you on a reef:
For many a Boat crew,
Must risk their lives,
All on the Sea rebel
By nights and by days.
The Sea by God's ordinance,
Consumes so many Men,
Who all together from the Fish,
Are then devoured,
But read! what depends on that,
Where our Bodies sail,
If God the soul then
Wants to preserve eternally.
What grief the Sailor suffers,
By nights and by day,
When he sees death before his eyes,
And may not escape:
Through storm and great thunder,
And the violence of the waves,
That brings us all the more
Into fear and great troubles.
Also great violence and adversity
The Sailor suffers valiantly,
From Turk and Pirates very fierce
They are assaulted,
And many more Enemies,
Who seek to harm them,
Who sail by the Sea,
May well think of that.
If they also on a lee shore
Are driven forward by storms,
Very quickly they cut away the Masts,
Then cut overboard,
Then we again see death,
Before our eyes with dread;
In short the care is great,
That the Sailor must bear,
God then helps her out of the distress,
Who calls to him deeply;
He does not want the Sinner's death,
But that he repents,
For by his strong hand,
He will revive the man again,
And brings her back to Land,
In a desired Harbor.
When they come ashore fine,
Their first work is,
Daily in brandy
But little in the Church,
It is quickly forgotten,
That the Lord has preserved her,
Faithfully helped by his Grace,
From fear and great terror.
When they receive their money in hand,
It is quickly consumed,
They buy therefore neither land nor sand,
The Landlady and Land,

With Ladies of the loose kind,

When the money is all spent,
It is no great honor to them,
Nor less for the women:
For they according to God's teaching,
Must keep themselves chaste.
But when, ah I do speak of,
What much display is seen,
Daily along the streets go,
Of daughters old and young,
In Holland everywhere,
One observes them flaunting,
It comes from misfortune,
They are no daughters with honor.
The Zeeland Girls, what a talk,
They know very well too,
At night to dance along the street,
Already with a Boat crew member,
And make a great commotion,
Wanting to know from the young men,
They are daughters of two houses,
Or I have forgotten it.
But it is with a foolish face,
Of these daughters here?
At night to dance over the street,
The musician leads the way,
It is no great honor to them,
They come to carry it lightly,
For in the East Indies far,
One hears about that.
The young men consider it no harm,
They say, it is pleasure,
To dance sometimes along the street,
Already with a Venus-animal,
But as the Scripture mentions
It is no honor to them,
That they their fair money,
So recklessly consume.
These young men and daughters fine,
They are very well known,
They live by the Turf quay,
Or somewhere nearby,
Because they are honest,
I do not want to blame them here,
For if the thread is not fine,
One would make it coarser.
You young men hear with good counsel,
Keep temperance in drinking,
For drunkenness, as it is said,
Is the mother of all evil,
Live free according to God's Teaching;
Want evil company hate,
So will God the Lord,
Let you sail in peace.
Farewell Sailor hear my admonition,
When you are in distress,
Call God the Lord from your heart,
Confess your great sins;
For he who from the heart truly
Repents of his sins,
Is healed by God the Lord
In all his wounds.
When we first found this new Song,
We sailed over Sea,
From East Indies to the Fatherland
To Middelburg the place,
With the Ship Prins Hendrik ree,
In the Year of thirty-nine,
And sixteen hundred plus,

['Mother, mother, why did my mother send me out?
There was no place to plant me, so why was I planted here?
After weeding one row, then two rows,
and two and a half rows in the Jangcheon field,
it was time for lunch.
Returning home,
I ate white porridge, then red bean porridge,
and at the end of the shelf in front of the ancestral tablet,
I wondered whether to eat or not eat that meal.
At that, the neighboring grandmother, hearing this,
said, "Chun-a, Chun-a, Okdang Chun-a, if that child belongs to the house, isn’t there a home?
If that is rice, isn’t there rice?"
Cutting and cutting off the hair, going to the temple,
hearing the neighbor’s grandmother’s words, I tore twelve pieces of cloth,
hung them up loosely, tore one piece to gather nuts,
two pieces to make a bag, and from the remaining cloth made a satin robe to wear.
Climbing the hill behind the village, the monk’s shoe strap broke,
so I asked for directions: "Please give me the way, the back gate, that way, please give me the way."
Looking along one side of the main gate, the young monk was sleeping,
the old monk did not answer, but there was also an old servant,
so I woke the young monk and told him,
"Please tie my hair, please tie my hair,
Please tie my hair tight,
If you tie it tight, at least say your name and surname."
After tying my hair into one headpiece,
the front of my hair was all wet.
After tying two bundles of hair, the front got wet with rain.
Wearing the monk’s robe, holding the wooden fish and rosary beads in my hand,
I crossed over and set out on a large road,
wearing a sky-like hat, riding a dragon-like horse,
coming along smoothly and nicely.
A person I did not know entered and stood still,
“Why? Why?”
My body felt as heavy as a thousand pounds.
“Why, monk’s robe? Why?”
"Why is this my wooden fish rosary like fire?"
Taking off the monk’s robe, I sat up, I sat up,
sat up on the embankment, sat up on the water fork embankment,
"Hurry and go, hurry and go, you must leave.
The three years of study, the studying for three years, now I am leaving after three years.
Running here and there, I can’t even run in the water."
Arriving at the gate in front of the house, the stone seat was wet,
this is the grace of the parents,
entered the room, as if asleep, gone.', "@Eoheoi Eoha
